content: Anti-patterns for SMB-facing web design studio sites: (1) Excessive 3D/WebGL everywhere — impressive to peers, intimidating/slow for a Berlin florist. (2) Showing only blue-chip logos in social proof — SMBs cannot identify with Cisco and IKEA. (3) Pricing hidden behind contact-only — SMBs need to know if they can afford it before investing time in a call. (4) Jargon-heavy copy (headless CMS, JAMstack) — creates distance. (5) No person/about section — SMBs hire people not brands. (6) Dark moody agency aesthetic that reads as very expensive or art project. (7) Overcomplicated navigation with no clear CTA. (8) No FAQ — pricing objections and turnaround time handled proactively converts faster.
